pt: {sc}abandon{/sc} {sc}desert{/sc} {sc}forsake{/sc} mean to leave without intending to return. {sc}abandon{/sc} suggests that the thing or person left may be helpless without protection.
{sc}desert{/sc} implies that the object left may be weakened but not destroyed by one's absence.
{sc}forsake{/sc} suggests an action more likely to bring impoverishment or bereavement to that which is forsaken than its exposure to physical dangers.

P. Ruelle points in a different direction, judging both the Old French noun {it}deserte{/it} and the adjective {it}desert{/it} as a variant of the past participle {it}deservi,{/it} descending from {it}*desérvitum,{/it} a presumed by-form of classical {it}dēservītum{/it} (see his "Notes sur le lexique des {it}Isopets,{/it}" {it}Romania,{/it} vol. 101, no. 401 [1980], pp. 77-78).
